cohort: 269 women with deliveries at <34 weeks gestation
finding: Implementation of a delayed cord clamping protocol for deliveries before 34 weeks gestation was not associated with an increase in adverse maternal outcomes, including estimated blood loss, postpartum hemorrhage, or transfusion rates.
mod_finding: An institutional delayed cord clamping protocol for deliveries <34 weeks was not associated with identifiable increases in adverse maternal outcomes.
